question: Which of the following statements is correct about the nature of the image formed by a concave mirror when the object is placed between the principal focus and the pole?
solution: The correct answer is __**Virtual, erect, magnified**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ • When an **object is placed between the principal focus (F) and the pole (P) of a concave mirror**, the image formed is **virtual, erect, and magnified**. This is a characteristic property of concave mirrors. • The **virtual image** is formed behind the mirror, as the reflected rays appear to diverge but actually meet when extended backward. • This type of image formation occurs because the object lies in the region where the reflected rays cannot converge on the real side, leading to a virtual formation. • **Magnification** happens as the object moves closer to the pole of the mirror, making the image larger than the object. • This phenomenon is utilized in devices like **shaving mirrors or makeup mirrors**, which need enlarged and upright images.
